sentences.text: The present appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the
appellant
/claimant

, challenging the award dated 29.06.2016, passed by the 3rd Additional Motor
Acciden

t Claims Tribunal, Indore, in Claim Case No.888/2015, whereby the learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim and awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.2,42,264/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

2. The factual matrix of the case is that on 27.03.2010 at around 12 pm, the injured met with an accident, as a result of which he sustained injuries on his right leg and also there is a fracture on tibia fabula bone and suffered 30% permanent disability.
The claimant filed a claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.17,50,000/-.

3. Learned claims Tribunal found that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.3, which was registered in the name NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:3404 2 MA-1881-2016 of respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No.1 on the fateful day.
After evaluating the ocular as well as documentary evidence, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,42,264/- in favour of the claimant considering the 9 percent permanent disability.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the Tribunal erred in assessing the appellant's income on the lower side and failed to properly appreciate the medical evidence regarding permanent disability.
It is further contended that the percentage of permanent disability has been assessed on the lower side.
Hence, the appellant prays for further enhancement of the award amount.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has supported the impugned award and submitted that the learned Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation to the claimant after duly considering the income of the claimant based on the material available on record.

He further argued that the owner of the offending vehicle had committed a breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, as the driver did not possess a valid and effective driving licence.

It is further submitted that since the present appeal was dismissed in the year 2016 and restored only in the year 2020, the appellant/claimant would not be entitled to interest part for a period of 1043 days.
6. I have heard the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7. It is not in dispute that respondent No.3 was responsible for causing the accident on the fateful day, the offending vehicle was insured with NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3404 3 MA-1881-2016 respondent No.1.
The only question for determination in this appeal is that whether the amount awarded by the Tribunal requires any modification or not?

6. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court found that the income of the claimant would be Rs.3950/- per month and therefore, the yearly income of the injured would come to Rs.47,400/- as per the guidelines of minimum wages.
This Court is further found that the learned Tribunal has rightly assessed the percentage of disability.

8. Therefore, after applying the law laid-down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 4 ACJ 270 and Sarla Verma &
Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Others reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the claimant is entitled to get the compensation as under:-
 Heads Compensation assess  Permanent disability Rs. 1,07,503/-
 Pain and suffering Rs. 25,000/-

Medical expenses Rs. 1,53,944/-
 Attender Rs. 10,000/-
 Special diet Rs. 10,000/-
 Transportation Rs. 10,000/-
Loss of income during treatment Rs. 10,000/-
 Future treatment Rs. 25,000/-

. Accordingly, this Court is of the considered opinion that the award passed by the learned Tribunal warrants interference, the appellant is entitled for enhancement for a sum of Rs 1,09,183/- and the enhanced amount shall also carry same interest as has been awarded by the Tribunal.

9. In view of the foregoing discussion, the appeal stands partly allowed and the impugned award is modified to the extent indicated herein above subject to following conditions:-
i. The respondent no.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against it.
ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee on the enhanced amount also, if required in the present case, within a period of 15 days from today.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed.
